item.content:encoded:
FOREX-Dollar hits 18-month high, then cools as investors await patient Fed Reuters | Updated: 15-10-2026 02:01 IST | Created: 15-10-2026 02:01 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The US dollar hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected US inflation data briefly revived expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike later this month, though the currency later pulled back as investors returned to expecting the Fed to be patient. The Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Wednesday that US consumer prices rose sharply in September as gasoline costs surged. "CPI is still making its way through valuations, and with stocks down we get another reason to bid up the USD a bit," said Marvin Loh, senior global market strategist at State Street in Boston. The US dollar index, a measure of the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 102.53 late on Wednesday afternoon, up 0.34%, after earlier trading as high as 102.94 late in the morning New York time. The report overshadowed recent dovish signals from Fed officials, including comments from New York Fed President John Williams that weakened the dollar in the previous session. On Thursday, Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman also signaled a wait-and-see approach before raising rates again. Meanwhile, the Fed's Beige Book showed on Wednesday that the US labor market remained in a low-hire, low-fire pattern, while inflation pressures picked up in parts of the country. "The Fed's dual mandate remains in tension with signs of labor market weakness," said Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management. "Tomorrow's releases should provide greater visibility into consumer conditions, the labor market, and price pressures through retail sales, initial jobless claims, and (producer price index)." Traders now see a 65% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, compared with 53% a month ago, while pricing in about 79 basis points of tightening by late 2027, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. The US central bank raised its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range last month. Michael Rosen, chief investment officer at Angeles Investments, said investors are losing confidence in the US's willingness to confront inflation. "We see ... a rising dollar being supported by higher interest rates," Rosen said. "Inflation won't fall unless the Fed engineers a recession by hiking rates significantly, or our policies on trade and immigration are corrected." EURO TROUBLES A host of global finance chiefs are in Bangkok, where the International Monetary Fund and World Bank are holding annual meetings. IMF fiscal affairs chief Rodrigo Valdes said the body has "dialed up" the urgency of its call for governments to rein in growing debts, while the IMF's Kristalina Georgieva said the US needs to make fiscal adjustments to put its debt on a more sustainable path. French bonds have been among the worst hit by a recent global selloff, with investors concerned that political jostling ahead of next year's presidential election may hinder efforts to reduce France's high deficit. The ECB's PresidentChristine Lagarde said at a CNN event in Bangkok that France should solve its debt woes through fiscal consolidation, damping speculation about whether the central bank might start buying French bonds to contain yields. The euro fell 0.41% to $1.1152, hitting a new 17-month low against the dollar and a fresh 16-month low versus sterling as a rise in oil prices and lingering concerns about France's fiscal health continued to weigh on the single currency. Roberto Mialich, FX strategist at UniCredit, said the euro could test $1.10 in the near term but was less bearish on the currency into year-end, expecting that "bond yield in the US will probably ease, although the situation in the euro zone could weigh on the euro." The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that British finance minister John Healey is expected to pay for all new giveaways in this month’s budget with higher taxes or spending cuts, rather than more borrowing. The IMF is not recommending that Britain speed up its fiscal consolidation, a senior official of the body said. Sterling fell 0.59% to $1.3177. Against the Japanese yen the dollar weakened 0.08% to 158.16.

item.title: India, Russia hold 7th round of 'Special Mechanism' talks on Pakistan and Afghanistan

item.content:encoded:
India, Russia hold 7th round of 'Special Mechanism' talks on Pakistan and Afghanistan India and Russia on Wednesday held the seventh round of talks under the India-Russia Special Mechanism on Pakistan and Afghanistan in New Delhi, reaffirming their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation under their Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 21:36 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 21:36 IST

Deputy National Security Adviser Pavan Kapoor, Russia’s Deputy Secretary of Security Council Aleksandr Venediktov (Photo/X/@MEAIndia). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India and Russia on Wednesday held the seventh round of talks under the India-Russia Special Mechanism on Pakistan and Afghanistan in New Delhi, reaffirming their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation under their Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. Ministry of External Affairs in a press release said that the talks were co-chaired by India's Deputy National Security Adviser Pavan Kapoor and Russia's Deputy Secretary of the Security Council Aleksandr Venediktov. According to the press release, the two sides held wide-ranging discussions on issues of common interest, including their implications for international security. “Both sides held wide-ranging discussions on issues of common interest, including their impact on international security. They reaffirmed their commitment to strengthen their ongoing cooperation under the aegis of ‘India-Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership’,” the press release stated. During his visit to New Delhi, Venediktov also called on National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, the Ministry said. The latest round of talks comes amid continued engagement between New Delhi and Moscow on regional security and broader strategic issues. Earlier on Wednesday, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar described India as a “natural option” for Russia as Moscow increasingly turns towards Asia amid strained relations with Europe. Speaking in a conversation with John Micklethwait, Editor-in-Chief of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, Jaishankar said Russia's relationship with Europe had deteriorated following the Russia-Ukraine war, prompting Moscow to strengthen its engagement with Asian countries. He emphasised that India-Russia relations had remained steady over the past 75-80 years and that maintaining these ties served the interests of both countries. “We are a natural option in that regard because we've had very decent relations with Russia from pretty much the early start,” Jaishankar said, adding that India wanted Russia to maintain meaningful relationships across Asia. The External Affairs Minister also highlighted the strategic significance of the partnership, stating that it had contributed to the balance of power and the overall status quo in Asia. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Pakistan: Karachi’s crime wave exposes public safety concerns after fatal robbery According to ARY News, in the latest incident, a young man was shot dead after resisting a robbery attempt in Shah Latif Town. Police said the victim was heading to work when armed suspects intercepted him and attempted to rob him. When he resisted, the assailants opened fire, leaving him critically injured. ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 17:43 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 17:43 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Karachi continues to grapple with persistent street crime, as armed robberies, fatal shootings and repeated attacks on ordinary citizens raise serious questions about the police’s ability and shoddy approach to ensure public safety, as reported by ARY News. According to ARY News, in the latest incident, a young man was shot dead after resisting a robbery attempt in Shah Latif Town. Police said the victim was heading to work when armed suspects intercepted him and attempted to rob him. When he resisted, the assailants opened fire, leaving him critically injured. He died while being taken to a nearby hospital. Police have registered a First Information Report (FIR) against unidentified suspects and launched an investigation. Meanwhile, another robbery was reported in Nazimabad No. 1, where two motorcycle-borne suspects targeted three residents sitting outside their homes. CCTV footage showed one suspect keeping the motorcycle running while his accomplice snatched mobile phones and other valuables from the victims. The robbers subsequently fled the scene. Police said they had received the footage and were in contact with the victims. Investigators believe the suspects can be identified from the recordings and are working to trace and arrest them. In a separate case near Shaheed-e-Millat Road, an online motorcycle rider was left devastated after two armed men allegedly robbed him of his mobile phone and cash at gunpoint. The rider stated that he had already been targeted in two previous robberies. The stolen phone had cost him Rs25,000, and he had purchased it only two months earlier, as highlighted by ARY News. Expressing concern about his livelihood, the rider questioned how he would afford another phone, which he needed to continue working and supporting his children. He appealed for justice, highlighting the financial and emotional toll of such crimes on working-class citizens, as reported by ARY News. (ANI)

item.title: Duane “Keffe D” Davis sentenced to 40 years of life imprisonment for orchestrating murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur
item.description: Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement.
item.content:encoded:
Duane “Keffe D” Davis sentenced to 40 years of life imprisonment for orchestrating murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement.  ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 09:51 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 09:51 IST

Duane “Keffe D” Davis faces sentence for Tupac Shakur murder (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

30 years after the death of rap icon Tupac Shakur in 1996, Duane “Keffe D” Davis has been sentenced to 40 years to life in a Nevada prison for orchestrating the killing, reported Variety. On Tuesday, Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement. Davis was facing a maximum of life in prison without parole. Prior to the judge’s decision, prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo pointed out a history of criminal activity and suggested that Davis “earned” the maximum sentence. “He’s an eight-time felon sitting before you on this crime perpetrated upon these family members, these family members, brothers. And you have to ask yourself, for this crime, for this person, what sentence does he deserve? Whatever your decision is, ultimately, in my mind, he deserves the maximum possible sentence because he’s earned it through his actions, his behaviour, and who he is as he stands here today,” he said, as quoted by Variety. Before handing down the sentence, Judge Carli Kierny went on to address Davis. “You don’t get to take a man from his family, you don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur. The world never forgot about him and his death, and you are going to face justice,” Kierny said, as quoted by People. Davis’ defence attorney Michael Sanft further claimed that they would appeal the judge’s decision, while Davis addressed the judge, asking for his “stuff back” that was taken from his home. In court, the late rapper’s sister, Sekyiwa Shakur and brother Maurice Shakur urged the judge to sentence Davis to the maximum punishment. “Tupac is truly my shining star, my shining prince; he is who God trusted to take care of me. My mother had two children, and God gave him to me, and he’s supposed to be my life partner. I spent 30 years without my protection. I believe that if any life mattered, if all life matters, for sure this man’s life mattered. I do believe when you take a life like that, you deserve every minute, every minute, of the maximum amount of punishment, time to sit down and contemplate what you’ve done to this world. He had so much promise, intentions for a better world for our people; he had plans and manifestos. He’s so much more than street violence,” Sekyiwa said as she struggled holding back tears. In late August, Davis was found guilty of murder with use of a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang. He was convicted after a weeks-long trial in Las Vegas, with prosecutors and police claiming that he orchestrated Shakur’s murder in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996. It was alleged that Davis handed the murder weapon to the gunman, believed to be either Davis’ nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson or another man in the car's back seat. Tupac Shakur was murdered in 1996 at a red light in Paradise, Nevada. He was shot four times, following which he succumbed to his injuries six days later. (ANI)
